subject: Subprocessor roster & EU logging vendor: data path and DPA clarifications

From: Sam Patel <sam@brightledger.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 04 Apr 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Quick ask: EU logging vendor & subprocessor list

Hi Lauren,

Hope you're well. We're doing a short compliance sweep before go-live in Amsterdam and need a few items from Redwood for our DPA team: a current subprocessor roster (including the EU logging vendor you mentioned in the RFC), the data flow for logs that include tenant identifiers, and any standardized attestation you can provide about temporary processors used for maintenance.

We're specifically concerned about:
- Where logs containing tenant IDs are stored (regional locus).
- Whether any logging/transit partners may replicate data outside the EU.
- Retention windows applied by downstream processors.

Can you share the roster and a short note we can add to our DPA? We're on a tight calendar; a response by EOD Fri (Apr 7) would be great.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Patel
Head of Infrastructure, BrightLedger

Thanks for the loop, Lauren. A couple of clarifying Qs for BrightLedger:
1) When you say "tenant identifiers" — are you referring to full PII-linked IDs or platform tenant IDs (hashed)? We need to scope whether pseudonymization applies.
2) Do you require an exportability statement (i.e., whether logs are ever routed to non-EU backup locations)? We can provide per-processor routing info but need to know the granularity you want in the DPA.

Ben (Sales Ops) — please prepare a short roster export with processor roles (logging, analytics, CDN, observability) and each processor's primary country. I can add a security note on encryption-in-transit and at-rest.

Rishi
Security Engineering — Redwood Inference

Hi all — apologies for the delayed reply; on the second question: yes, an explicit exportability line would be helpful (we tag processors as "EU-only" or "may replicate outside EU").

On identifiers: platform tenant IDs (hashed) are fine — we do not need PII-level detail. Retention: if you can confirm the default retention window the logging vendor enforces and whether we can request shorter windows per contract, that would be ideal.

I've attached a preliminary roster (internal) for context — it has our current vendors and what they asked for.

Thanks,
Sam

Date: Sun, 07 Apr 2028 16:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick ask: EU logging vendor & subprocessor list

Sam — thanks, attached is the packet we promised. Summary of what we shared: 
- Attachment: bl_subprocessor_roster_20280405.xlsx — list of Redwood subprocessors relevant to BrightLedger (roles + primary country).
- Attachment: redwood_dpa_redline_v1.pdf — suggested DPA clause with exportability language and retention defaults for logging vendors.
- Short attestation text in the packet: temporary maintenance processors are allowed only under documented change control, with RBAC-limited keys and full audit trails; any temporary access is timeboxed and logged.

Short answers: 
- Logs with tenant IDs are retained in EU regions by the logging vendor (primary locus Netherlands). No routine replication outside the EU for production logs; there is optional cross-region backup for disaster recovery which is explicitly flagged in our roster as "may replicate outside EU" and requires customer consent.
- Default retention for tenant-identifiable logs at the logging vendor is 90 days; per-account shorter retention can be requested and is typically achievable via contract addendum (we attached language).

Next steps: 
1) Review the roster and redline PDF; if BrightLedger wants a contract addendum for a stricter retention window, loop in your procurement and we'll fast-track a DPA amendment.
2) Rishi/Naomi — if you both OK the attestation wording I'll sign off and share a final version signed by Redwood legal.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Account Sales — Redwood Inference
